span: maintenance awarded to the aggrieved woman under the D.V. is in addition to an order of maintenance provided u/S. 125 Cr.P.C.
why: Concerns overlap between maintenance under the DV Act, HMA and s.125 for a wife, not a divorced wife's entitlement.

span: The husband being an able-bodied person is duty bound to maintain his wife who is unable to maintain herself
why: About a husband's duty to maintain his wife during marriage; no divorced wife is in issue.

span: The law presumes in favour of marriage and against concubinage when a man and woman have cohabited continuously
why: Headnote on the presumption of marriage for a wife, not a divorced wife.

span: this Court can depart from the procedure as well as the substantive laws
why: Answers the Article 142 reference on divorce by consent; s.125 appears only as connected proceedings that can be quashed.

span: a divorced Muslim woman would only be entitled to maintenance as provided in Section 3(1) of the 1986 Act for Muslim Women, notwithstanding any other law including Section 125 of the Cr.PC
why: Headnote says s.125 claims are decided by Family Courts and divorced Muslim women are not shut out, yet describes the non-obstante clause as limiting them to the 1986 Act; the headnote is internally mixed on whether s.125 remains available.
